news.headline: A Spacecraft Blasts Off to Visit the Moons of Mars
news.body: Japan's space agency launched a spacecraft called MMX on a giant H3 rocket. It is headed for Mars, where it will study the planet's two lumpy, potato-shaped moons, Phobos and Deimos. The plan is to land on Phobos twice, scoop up a little bit of its soil, and bring it back to Earth in 2031. A small rover from France and Germany will ride along, too. Scientists hope the soil will solve a big mystery: where did Mars get its moons?

news.headline: A 6-Year-Old Finds a Super-Rare Fossil
news.body: Leo, a 6-year-old from Nebraska, flipped over a big rock at a state park, hoping to find a fossil. He found something much rarer: the print of a conulariid, an ancient sea animal shaped like an upside-down pyramid. These soft, jellyfish-like creatures lived hundreds of millions of years ago and almost never turned into fossils. It is the first one found in Nebraska in more than 55 years! The fossil will stay at the park so other kids can learn from it.

news.headline: Eight Capybara Babies Draw Record Crowds
news.body: A wildlife park on the Isle of Man, an island between England and Ireland, welcomed eight capybara pups! Two moms had their babies just days apart. So many people came to see them that the park had its busiest October weekend ever. Capybaras come from South America and love wet, marshy places. The park says the cute pups are helping visitors learn why wetlands are so important for animals and people.
